title: Maintaining Design Consistency with UX Engine
summary: This reel demonstrates how to prevent design drift in AI-generated interfaces by using a design system skill. It explains how extracting existing tokens from code ensures that every new screen adheres to a single, coherent visual language.

transcript.text: Ten AI-built pricing pages. One of them used UX Engine.
Three screens. Three blues, three button styles.
Nothing carries between generations, so every screen decides alone and your product stops looking like one product.
Use the design-system skill on your project. It writes one file at the root, and every other skill then reads it.
Rule zero: it reads your Tailwind config, your CSS variables, then your most reused component, because if you already made those decisions, the system already exists.
Eleven tokens extracted, none invented, each carrying the one line reason it's there.
After that, a new blue gets stopped and replaced by the closest token. Extensions are allowed, but they get written down with their reason, because silent invention is how drift starts.
Coherent still isn't distinctive. The other new skill forces one decision per axis. Type, colour, space, finish, and it refuses to let you ship a default.
UX Engine 2.0. Eight skills, two of them new, two sub-agents, four commands for Claude Code. $79 instead of $99 until Thursday night. Link in bio.

before_after: Inconsistent UI screens with varying colors and button styles are transformed into a unified product interface by extracting and enforcing a shared design system.
